$note: Corpus for the tier-2 collapse-duplicate-avatar-rolls differential (P4.D184,
v4 7fbf8a55b; grown for bug 145 at v4 23abc1ba1, P4.D192). Read by BOTH
sides: harness/oracle/cases/avatar-rolls-collapse-heal.test.ts drives v4's
REAL migration + REAL ledger write, and
crates/quilltap-harness/tests/avatar_rolls_collapse_heal_equivalence.rs drives
quilltap_core::db::avatar_rolls_collapse_heal over the same seeds.
Scenarios 1-13 are v4's OWN thirteen test cases from
__tests__/unit/migrations/collapse-duplicate-avatar-rolls.test.ts, rebuilt as
data so the two implementations walk identical state. Four more (14-17) ask
the questions v4's suite does not: the cross-app ledger row, a pass with
nothing to collapse, a roll whose storageKey names no blob, and a null model.
18-24 are bug 145's shapes (v4 23abc1ba1). TWO of v4's six new cases are NOT
here, because the corpus already had them: its `reports the rolls it kept`
and its census `says nothing about a duplicate it chose to keep` seed exactly
what scenario 9 seeds, so scenario 9 carries both — the port moves its
`message` (the kept clause) and its `warns` stay empty. And v4's census case
is an EARLY-RETURN pass (one roll, no victims), so three of these ask what
v4's own suite never opens: 22 the post-summary census exit, 23 the
!isPhotosRelativePath conjunct (an album link in the roll's OWN mount, seeded
FIRST — the mount conjunct alone saves v4's `vault-1` cases), and 24 a
non-zero `protectedKept` in the summary log bag (v4's protected case takes
the early return, where no summary line is emitted at all).
A roll seeds a `files` row PLUS its vault file/blob/link/chunk, exactly as
v4's `seedRoll` does. `noBlob: true` seeds the files row alone. `albumLinks`
is v4's `keepInAlbum`: a SECOND link over the SAME content row, at
photos/kept-<id>.webp, in `vault-1` unless the entry names a mount.

P4.D203 (v4 186eb09cb/f45a517a9): the scenario `repoints-a-lantern-announcement-whose-text-is-a-compressed-blob` is the boot heal's codec proof. `chat_messages.content` and `opaqueContent` are REGISTERED COMPRESSED COLUMNS, so at the target pin v4 stores both of this message's 2 KB bodies as brotli BLOBs. v4's migration reads them through `qt_text()` and writes them back through `textToBlob()` (`collapse-duplicate-avatar-rolls-v1.ts:497-508,556-561`); v5 had neither, so its `Option<String>` bind raised `InvalidColumnType` and the `?` aborted the whole BOOT pass — this heal is the FIRST thing that broke on a migrated instance, at startup. The inline uuid sits in the MIDDLE of the long body, so the substitution must survive a decode/re-encode round trip.
